label: Proton proton I chain context
adaptation_note: Two explicitly distinct precursor sequences, both helium-3 inputs and a final product frame preserve all nucleon counts and emitted-particle codes. Each nucleus box is an introduced membership cue, not a shell.
acceptance_requirement: Retain proton/neutron counts, emitted-particle identities and the multiplicity of the two precursor paths. Do not collapse two reactions into one unexplained branch.

frames.title: Precursor A: two protons to deuterium
frames.teaching_key: Branch A, first reaction: two free protons (circles) yield one deuteron containing one proton and one neutron (square), plus one positron (diamond above) and one electron neutrino (triangle below). The other branch repeats this reaction independently; do not count it as a repeated view of the same nucleus. Box groups a nucleus; it is not a physical shell.

frames.title: Precursor A: deuterium plus proton
frames.teaching_key: Branch A, second reaction: the deuteron (one circle, one square) combines with one additional free proton to give helium-3 (two circles and one square) and one gamma photon (zigzag below arrow). This happens once in each branch. Group boxes are nucleus membership cues, not atom shells.

frames.title: Precursor B: two protons to deuterium
frames.teaching_key: Branch B, first reaction: two free protons (circles) yield one deuteron containing one proton and one neutron (square), plus one positron (diamond above) and one electron neutrino (triangle below). The other branch repeats this reaction independently; do not count it as a repeated view of the same nucleus. Box groups a nucleus; it is not a physical shell.

frames.title: Precursor B: deuterium plus proton
frames.teaching_key: Branch B, second reaction: the deuteron (one circle, one square) combines with one additional free proton to give helium-3 (two circles and one square) and one gamma photon (zigzag below arrow). This happens once in each branch. Group boxes are nucleus membership cues, not atom shells.

frames.title: Combine both helium-3 nuclei
frames.teaching_key: The two boxed groups are the distinct helium-3 nuclei from precursor branches A and B: each has two protons and one neutron. Their paths converge toward the next product frame. Both precursor branches are required; no nucleus is omitted. Grouping is diagrammatic, not a measured particle configuration.

frames.title: Helium-4 and two returned protons
frames.teaching_key: Products of the preceding fusion: helium-4 box contains two protons (circles) and two neutrons (squares); the two separate circles to the right are returned free protons. Across both precursor paths six protons entered and two return: net four protons converted to helium-4, with two positrons, two electron neutrinos and two gamma emissions shown in the precursor steps. Positron annihilation, energies and other pp branches are outside this selected diagram.
